correctness.rationale: For the explicit \(\mathbf Q\)-example, the two graph maps have degrees \(1\) and \(2\), so their graph classes are \(f+h\) and \(2f+h\). Their equality determinant is \(u^3+uv^2+v^3\); dehomogenization gives \(t^3+t+1\), which has no rational root and discriminant \(-31\). Thus the collision scheme is one degree-three closed point over \(\mathbf Q\) and three reduced points over \(\mathbf C\). Inclusion-exclusion gives \(\chi_c=4-2-2+3=3\), excluding \(\mathbf A^2\), whose compactly supported Euler characteristic is \(1\). For the general necessity, base change turns any affine-space complement into affine space and the projective-bundle inclusion-exclusion formula makes the Euler characteristic equal to the number of geometric collision points, forcing one; characteristic zero then forces that point to be rational. For sufficiency, once the collision point is rational, every center in the ruled-surface construction is defined over the base field and the final affine bundles over affine space are trivial.

value.rationale: The initiating theorem is advertised over arbitrary fields and is used as a geometric recognition criterion for affine space. Confusing one closed point with one geometric or rational point changes the answer, even in the smallest surface case. The explicit \(\mathbf Q\)-example gives a reusable diagnostic and the corrected characteristic-zero formulation states exactly what descent data are needed. This is a substantive boundary clarification rather than a renaming or routine numerical special case.
